details:
Joystick drifting is a major problem. It makes the game less immersive and more annoying. To combat this, I have some recommendations for settings that would improve user experience. These changes will focus on the joystick for VR users.

Firstly, a setting changes to the Action Menu. Because of joystick drift, it becomes almost insufferable to use the Action Menu. For this, I have a major setting I would recommended adding. Be able to swap the Joystick Action Menu with the Hand Tracking Action Menu. The Hand Tracking Action Menu instead of using the joystick, it uses trigger clicks. I believe if you gave the option to be able to switch the Joystick Action Menu with the Hand Tracking Action Menu it would fix the Action Menu for many VR users.

Secondly, another setting change that would make joystick drift less annoying is a change to the Quick Menu. A major problem VR users have with the Quick Menu is when they move it closes. This makes it annoying to use certain features on the Quick Menu due to joystick drifting. Because every time you open the Quick Menu your joystick can drift and close the menu entirely. To fix this, I would recommend adding a setting that would remove being able to close the Quick Menu by moving.

The last change I would recommend is about being able to turn off your joysticks and replace your movement with the controller buttons. This wouldn't just be turning off joystick turning only, it would also be about replacing joystick movement with button movement. To do this, you can add a setting where you can toggle if your joysticks can use movement and turning. Then, be able to replace the movement with a click of a button that moves you forward in either hand or head direction. I Believe this change would directly fix joystick drifting for VR Users.

In conclusion, I believe these changes would improve on controlling joystick drift for VR Users. It allows the said users to be less annoyed and more immersed in VRChat. If these changes were added to the settings, it would greatly improve on the VR player base.
title: Major Recommendations to Setting Changes for VR Users
